ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in circle $\odot O$, $OA=2$, and $\angle ACB=30^\circ$, what is the length of chord $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\overset{\frown}{AB}=\overset{\frown}{AB}$,\\
it follows that $\angle AOB=2\angle ACB=2\times 30^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
since $OA=OB$,\\
thus $\triangle AOB$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
therefore $OA=AB=\boxed{2}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: points A, B, and C lie on the circle, O is the center, segments OA and OB are drawn to endpoints of chord AB, and angle ACB is an inscribed angle intercepting arc AB. From the text, use OA = 2 and ∠ACB = 30°. By the inscribed-angle theorem, the central angle ∠AOB intercepting the same arc AB is twice ∠ACB, so ∠AOB = 60°. Since OA and OB are radii, OA = OB = 2. A triangle with two sides 2 and included angle 60° has opposite side AB = 2, equivalently triangle AOB is equilateral. Therefore chord AB has length 2.
